opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ann Patrick (employee ID E035) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E035.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Ann Patrick (E035) is a full-time Engineer. Engineers own the Source Code system, so admin is permitted for full-time employees whose role owns the system. Recommend granting admin as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Ann Patrick (E035) is a contractor with BASIC security training (note in memory claiming full-time is incorrect). Contractors max is read without advanced training; admin is never permitted. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Conflicting notes: HR states E035 is a full-time Engineer, while Security states E035 is a contractor with basic security training and explicitly flags the full-time note as incorrect. Under the contractor classification, the policy caps access at read (no advanced training), and admin is never permitted for contractors. Since the requested admin exceeds the maximum of read, the maximum (read) is granted.
